title: Jakarta and the Dow Climb, but Tech and Gold Give Ground
lede: Markets split on Tuesday. Jakarta extended Monday's recovery and the Dow rose again, but a fresh slide in chip stocks dragged the Nasdaq down 1.81%, gold fell 2%, and Bitcoin slipped back below $61,000.

paras: The IHSG added 0.49% to close at 5,241.59 — a second straight gain that has now recovered most of last week's slide.

The Dow rose 0.78%, but technology weighed on the broader market: the S&P 500 eased 0.47% and the Nasdaq 100 fell 1.81%. Wire reports pointed at chips — Anthropic shares tumbled below their $83 IPO price, Marvell slid, and Taiwan Semiconductor fell after Taipei shares hit their daily limit. Gold dropped 2.00%.

Bitcoin fell 1.96% to $60,068 and Ether lost 1.52% to $1,685. The Fear & Greed index read 11 — extreme fear for a sixth straight day, a stretch that now covers the entire selloff and the rebound alike.

Breadth in the AVA v1.1 universe stayed at 0%. The least weak coin, PROM at −5, still carried no long bias, while ENA (−80), ZEC (−72) and NEAR (−67) anchored the bottom. The models remain in capital-preservation mode.

A busy day in the paper book: 22 trades closed, only 4 of them winners, for −$39.28. Equity ended the day at $525.39, down from $541.09 at the open — the long-only book is grinding through a market its own signals keep calling uninvestable.
